source_text: Πᾶς δὲ προφήτης ἀληθινὸς θέλων καθῆσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄξιός ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ. ὡσαύτως διδάσκαλος ἀληθινός ἐστιν ἄξιος καὶ αὐτὸς ὥσπερ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ. πᾶσαν οὖν ἀπαρχὴν γεννημάτων ληνοῦ καὶ ἅλωνος, βοῶν τε καὶ προβάτων λαβὼν δώσεις τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῖς προφήταις: αὐτοὶ γάρ εἰσιν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ὑμῶν. ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἔχητε προφήτην, δότε τοῖς πτωχοῖς. ἐὰν σιτίαν ποιῇς, τὴν ἀπαρχὴν λαβὼν δὸς κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν. ὡσαύτως κεράμιον οἴνου ἡ ἐλαίου ἀνοίξας, τὴν ἀπαρχὴν λαβὼν δὸς τοῖς προφήταις: ἀργυρίου δὲ καὶ ἱματισμοῦ καὶ παντὸς κτήματος λαβὼν τὴν ἀπαρχήν, ὡς ἄν σοι δόξῃ, δὸς κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν.
pass_a_gloss: Every true prophet wanting to sit with you is worthy of his food. Similarly, a true teacher is also worthy, just like the worker, of his food. Therefore, taking every firstfruit of the products of the winepress and the threshing floor, of oxen and sheep, you will give the firstfruit to the prophets: for they are your high priests. But if you do not have a prophet, give to the poor. If you make a batch of dough, taking the firstfruit, give according to the command. Similarly, when you open a jar of wine or oil, taking the firstfruit, give to the prophets: and of silver and clothing and every possession, taking the firstfruit, as it seems good to you, give according to the command.
pass_b_english: Any true prophet who wants to stay among you deserves his keep. Likewise, a true teacher is just as worthy of his food as any laborer. So set aside the first portion of everything your winepress and threshing floor produce, and the firstborn of your cattle and flocks, and give those firstfruits to the prophets — they are your high priests. If you have no prophet, give them to the poor instead. When you bake bread, take the first portion of the dough and give it as the command directs. The same goes for wine and oil: when you open a jar, set aside the first portion and give it to the prophets. And from your silver, your clothing, and every other possession, take the firstfruits as you see fit, and give them according to the command.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The distinction between 'wanting to sit with you' (Pass A) and 'wants to stay among you' (Pass B) for καθῆσθαι is acceptable. The translation of the list of firstfruits (winepress, threshing floor, oxen, sheep, silver, clothing, possessions) is complete and faithful.
